title: InfraMLForge: Developer Tooling for Rapid LLM Development and Scalable Deployment

live_model.evidence: "GPT-4 (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)...achieved a remarkable average performance of 85.5" (Sec. V-A); Table I's matching row (85.5) is labeled "GPT-4o" instead

prompt.note: No prompt text or template is shown; the paper is abstract formalism (a "representation matrix", dataset versioning function, deployment DAG) with no described prompting method.

claim.metric: Overall Avg. performance across EPIE, CLIMATE-FEVER, SkillSpan, NLPeer
claim.location: Table I -- row labeled "GPT-4o" (not "GPT-4 Turbo"), contradicting the body text's claim that this is GPT-4-turbo-2024-04-09's result

data.source: EPIE, CLIMATE-FEVER, SkillSpan, NLPeer are named public datasets, but no per-dataset item counts or splits are given

notes: The paper internally contradicts itself: body text attributes the 85.5 result to "GPT-4 (gpt-4-turbo-2024-04-09)", but Table I's row for that value is labeled "GPT-4o". Combined with baselines that are non-sequiturs for the stated NLP tasks (e.g. "Non-Prehensile Tool-Object Manipulation", a robotics-grasping method, listed as a text-processing baseline) and a Research Square preprint with no peer review, this reads as templated/low-credibility content rather than a verifiable experiment; no reliable number can be tied to a specific live model.
